policy: Bandit metrics._totals.skipped_tests must exactly match this ratchet; every reduction updates the baseline in the same commit and increases are forbidden.

debt_plan.rule: Do not bulk-remove suppressions; preserve identifier validation and add focused tests before each removal.

_execute_allowed_git_command()'s B603 (subprocess.check_output, line ~80) already runs with an absolute, shutil.which-resolved git binary, a fixed 10s timeout, shell=False, and an argv gated by _is_allowed_git_command()'s explicit allowlist (six fixed command tuples plus one validated 'git checkout -- <ref>' shape, with a NUL-byte rejection check). tests/unit/web/routes/test_project_ops_helpers.py already pins the exact allowlisted/rejected argvs and the fail-closed no-op when git cannot be resolved to an absolute path. Removing the nosec was verified to reproduce the same B603 finding described in the other reviews (Bandit flags any non-literal subprocess argv regardless of how it was built); no code change removes the need for the suppression without dropping the allowlisted git lookups this route depends on.

New shared wrapper (run_trusted_command/popen_trusted_command) introduced to structurally shrink this ratchet: every reviewed B603 call site so far (four reviews above) already used a fixed/validated argv yet still reproduced B603 the moment its nosec was removed -- Bandit flags any non-literal subprocess argv regardless of how safely it was constructed, so per-call-site nosecs were never going to collapse toward the 2027-04-30/20 and 2027-07-31/0 targets through individual review alone. This module centralizes the audited subprocess.run/Popen call to exactly two lines (one nosec each; kept, unavoidable for the same reason as the other reviews) so every caller carries zero nosec of its own. Phase 1 migrated 8 low-risk call sites to it: scripts/ci/check_ruff_debt_baseline.py, scripts/doctor_production_readiness.py, scripts/sync_postgres_password.py, launcher/process.py, core/doctor/__init__.py (x2), core/multimodal.py (x2), main.py (x3) -- 13 individual suppressions removed, 2 added here, net -11 (verified via bandit -r . before/after each migration). tools/audit_imports.py was deliberately left unmigrated: it has no sys.path setup and no established precedent of importing from core/, so its invocation context (bare `python tools/audit_imports.py`) is not guaranteed to have the repo root on sys.path -- the risk of breaking a standalone dev tool for one suppression wasn't worth it. 100% covered by tests/unit/core/test_trusted_subprocess.py (shell=True rejection, empty-command rejection, embedded-NUL rejection, and the happy path for both run and Popen). Full-repo Bandit skipped_tests dropped 39 -> 30 in this phase; maximum_skipped_tests ratcheted down in the same commit per policy. Remaining B603 sites (managers/code/*, web/plugins/sandbox.py, web/process_lifecycle.py, managers/system_health.py, tools/audit_imports.py) are planned for later phases of the same migration, in ascending order of risk.

Phase 2 of the same migration: 6 medium-risk call sites moved to run_trusted_command()/popen_trusted_command() -- managers/code/linter_runners.py, managers/code/runner.py, managers/code/test_runner_orchestrator.py, managers/code_manager.py (x2: subprocess.run + subprocess.Popen), managers/system_health.py, web/process_lifecycle.py. 7 individual suppressions removed, 0 added (wrapper already existed from Phase 1) -- net -7. web/process_lifecycle.py's call needed a real behavior-preserving adjustment, not just a rename: it used subprocess.check_output() (returns bytes directly), which the wrapper doesn't expose -- rewritten as run_trusted_command(..., stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, check=True).stdout, the documented equivalent, verified against its existing tests (tests/unit/web/test_runtime_helpers.py, tests/unit/root/test_web_server.py) with no change. Also fixed a real mypy strict regression the migration introduced in managers/system_health.py (run_trusted_command's necessarily-generic CompletedProcess[Any] return type turned `result.stdout.strip()` into an Any-return where the function is annotated -> str; wrapped with str(...), matching the same idiom already used in core/multimodal.py's _run_subprocess_capture). managers/code/docker.py's execute_code_with_docker_cli(run_command=subprocess.run) was deliberately left alone: it's docker-execution-adjacent (grouped with Phase 3's docker_lifecycle.py/sandbox.py) and, since Bandit's B603 pattern-matches only literal `subprocess.X(...)` call expressions, this dependency-injected default doesn't even carry a nosec today -- nothing to reduce here, and touching it now would blur the Phase 2/3 risk boundary agreed with the user. Full-repo Bandit skipped_tests dropped 30 -> 23; maximum_skipped_tests ratcheted down in the same commit per policy. Remaining B603/B102 sites (web/plugins/sandbox.py, managers/code/docker_lifecycle.py, tools/audit_imports.py) are Phase 3, planned as a separate PR given the higher stakes.

Phase 3 (the higher-stakes plugin-sandbox/Docker-lifecycle batch, done as its own careful pass per the user's request): DockerPluginSandboxBackend.request()'s 3 B603 sites (docker create/start/rm) migrated to run_trusted_command() -- same unavoidable-B603 reasoning as every prior review, all three already ran with fixed argv built entirely from this module's own _isolation_argv()/_create_command() constants plus a container_id captured from a prior trusted call, never from plugin-controlled input. Verified against the full existing test suite (tests/unit/web/plugins/test_sandbox.py), including its extensive `monkeypatch.setattr("web.plugins.sandbox.subprocess.run", ...)` mocks -- these patch the real subprocess module's run attribute (not a stand-in namespace), so they kept intercepting the wrapper's internal subprocess.run call unchanged (same mechanism already confirmed for main.py's tests in Phase 1). Live Docker-daemon integration tests (tests/integration/web/test_plugin_sandbox_container_escape.py, test_plugin_sandbox_integration.py) could not be run in this environment (no Docker daemon available) -- they don't mock sandbox.py's subprocess calls at all (they run real containers), so the migration is behaviorally transparent to them, but this is recorded as an honest gap rather than a claimed verification. The separate B102 (`exec(code, namespace)` in execute_validated_plugin_source(), line ~483) is NOT a subprocess concern and out of this wrapper's scope entirely -- kept, unavoidable: it's the entire purpose of the explicitly legacy, fail-closed, opt-in-only in-process plugin backend (assert_in_process_plugin_execution_allowed() refuses it outright in production and without an explicit env opt-in). Defense-in-depth is already maximized around it: validate_plugin_source() statically blocks dangerous imports/calls/introspection via AST walk before this line is ever reached, and build_restricted_plugin_builtins() strips exec/eval/compile/open/etc. from the runtime __builtins__ the executed code actually sees. Removing exec() here would remove the feature (running plugin source) it exists to provide; no safe reduction exists.

The module's `# nosec B404` on its own `import subprocess` line was left as-is (harmless and doesn't count toward skipped_tests -- B404 is already globally skipped via pyproject.toml's bandit.skips).

Phase 1 deliberately left this file unmigrated because it lacked any sys.path setup and a bare `python tools/audit_imports.py` invocation was empirically confirmed (this review) to NOT have the repo root on sys.path (Python puts the script's own directory, tools/, on sys.path[0] for a direct script invocation) -- `import core` would have failed silently for that invocation style.
